# Metrics: lifecycle numbers for spoke

Run every command from the repo root. Each command prints the number next to it. The commands use `bun -e` and `git` only.

## DORA keys

Source: `data/deploys.csv` (69 rows, all `service=spoke`) and `data/incidents.csv` (9 rows). Both files are plain CSV: no quotes, no commas inside fields, and the same number of fields on every row.

| Key | Value | Command |
|---|---|---|
| Deployment frequency, total | 69 deploys | `bun -e 'const r=require("fs").readFileSync("data/deploys.csv","utf8").trim().split("\n").slice(1).map(l=>l.split(","));const t=r.map(x=>Date.parse(x[4])).sort((a,b)=>a-b);const w=(t.at(-1)-t[0])/6048e5;console.log(r.length+" deploys, "+w.toFixed(2)+" weeks, "+(r.length/w).toFixed(2)+" per week")'` |
| Deployment frequency, per week | 2.68 per week (69 deploys over 25.71 weeks, first to last `deployed_at`) | same command as above |
| Lead time for changes | 66.02 h median, `committed_at` to `deployed_at`, over 69 deploys | `bun -e 'const r=require("fs").readFileSync("data/deploys.csv","utf8").trim().split("\n").slice(1).map(l=>l.split(","));const h=r.map(x=>(Date.parse(x[4])-Date.parse(x[3]))/36e5).sort((a,b)=>a-b);const n=h.length;console.log("median lead time "+(n%2?h[(n-1)/2]:(h[n/2-1]+h[n/2])/2).toFixed(2)+" h over "+n+" deploys")'` |
| Change failure rate | 13.0% (9 of 69 deploys have an `incident_id`) | `bun -e 'const r=require("fs").readFileSync("data/deploys.csv","utf8").trim().split("\n").slice(1).map(l=>l.split(","));const f=r.filter(x=>x[5].trim()).length;console.log(f+" of "+r.length+" deploys = "+(100*f/r.length).toFixed(1)+"%")'` |
| Time to restore | 3.52 h median, `started_at` to `resolved_at`, over 9 incidents | `bun -e 'const r=require("fs").readFileSync("data/incidents.csv","utf8").trim().split("\n").slice(1).map(l=>l.split(","));const h=r.map(x=>(Date.parse(x[3])-Date.parse(x[2]))/36e5).sort((a,b)=>a-b);const n=h.length;console.log("median time to restore "+(n%2?h[(n-1)/2]:(h[n/2-1]+h[n/2])/2).toFixed(2)+" h over "+n+" incidents")'` |

## This feature, from git

Range: every commit from the root commit `20a20b3` up to and including `52122d2` ("approve: work/intent/next-dedupe-wrenches.md by pm"). That is 30 commits, and `52122d2` is HEAD. Every command below names `52122d2`, so commits added later do not change the numbers.

| Measure | Value | Command |
|---|---|---|
| Intent to spec | 27.50 h: `6160dd5` changed `work/intent.md` first (2026-10-27 11:30 UTC); `62811fb` changed `work/spec.md` first (2026-10-28 15:00 UTC). Both use author date. | `bun -e 'const g=p=>require("child_process").execSync("git log --reverse --format=%at 52122d2 -- "+p).toString().split("\n")[0];console.log(((g("work/spec.md")-g("work/intent.md"))/3600).toFixed(2)+" h")'` |
| First plan commit (used in the next row) | `b8534f5`, the only commit that changed `work/plan.md` | `git log --reverse --format='%h %aI %s' 52122d2 -- work/plan.md` |
| Spec commits after the first plan commit | 0 | `git rev-list --count b8534f5..52122d2 -- work/spec.md` |
| Files outside plan.md | 0. P-1, P-2 and P-3 changed 2 files, `src/wrenches.ts` and `src/crew-queue.ts`, and `work/plan.md` names both. | `bun -e 'const x=c=>require("child_process").execSync(c).toString();const named=new Set([...x("cat work/plan.md").matchAll(/\x60([^\x60]+)\x60/g)].map(m=>m[1]));const files=new Set(x("git log --format= --name-only --grep=^P- 52122d2").split("\n").filter(Boolean));const out=[...files].filter(f=>!named.has(f));console.log(out.length+" outside plan.md, of "+files.size+" files changed by P- commits",out)'` |
| Share of commits with the `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailer | 60.0% (18 of 30 commits) | `bun -e 'const l=require("child_process").execFileSync("git",["log","--format=%h%x09%(trailers:key=Co-Authored-By,valueonly,separator=;)","52122d2"]).toString().trim().split("\n");const c=l.filter(x=>/\tClaude\b/.test(x)).length;console.log(c+" of "+l.length+" commits = "+(100*c/l.length).toFixed(1)+"%")'` |
| Median commit size | 16 lines added plus deleted, over 29 commits (skips the root commit `20a20b3`) | `bun -e 'const o=require("child_process").execSync("git log --reverse --format=@%h --numstat 52122d2").toString().split("@").slice(1).map(s=>s.trim().split("\n").slice(1).filter(Boolean).reduce((t,l)=>{const [a,d]=l.split("\t");return t+(a==="-"?0:+a)+(d==="-"?0:+d)},0));const s=o.slice(1).sort((a,b)=>a-b),n=s.length;console.log("median "+(n%2?s[(n-1)/2]:(s[n/2-1]+s[n/2])/2)+" lines over "+n+" commits (first skipped)")'` |

Notes on the git numbers:

- The "P- commits" filter uses `--grep=^P-`, which matches any line of a message. Here it matches only the 3 subjects `P-1`, `P-2` and `P-3`. To check: `git log --format='%h %s' --grep=^P- 52122d2`. The `A-1` commits from the postmortem fix are not P- commits, so they are not counted.
- The range has no binary files, so numstat has no `-` rows to treat as 0.
- 9 of the 29 sized commits change 1 line. They are mostly `approve:` commits that add one row to `work/approvals.jsonl`. These commits pull the median down, so 16 lines describes the mix of commits, not a typical code change.
- The trailer share counts every commit in the range. That includes the root commit and the 11 `approve:` commits, which people made and which have no trailer.

## What these numbers do not prove

**A comparison with DORA.** The change failure rate of 13.0% falls between the "high" (10%) and "medium" (15%) groups in the DORA 2023 State of DevOps report. The "elite" group is at 5%. That ranking holds only if our definition matches DORA's, and it does not quite match. Here a deploy counts as failed only if a row in `incidents.csv` names it. DORA also counts deploys that needed a rollback, hotfix or patch without a formal incident. A rollback with no incident would never appear in this file. So 13.0% is a floor on the true rate. Also, DORA defines its groups from survey answers in ranges, and 9 failures out of 69 is a small sample: one more incident would raise the rate to 14.5%.

**What one feature cannot show.**

- **No comparison.** There is one feature and no baseline. Nothing tells us whether 27.5 h from intent to spec, 0 spec changes after the plan, or 0 files outside the plan is good, typical or lucky. Measuring that needs the same numbers for features built without this workflow, or for many features built with it.
- **The two halves never meet.** The deploy commits in `data/deploys.csv` (for example `de99423` and `afd5991`) do not exist in this repo's history. `deploys.csv` ends on 2026-10-31, before `work/rollout.yaml` was approved on 2026-11-01. This feature's own lead time, failure and restore time are not part of the DORA numbers yet.
- **Following the plan does not mean the result is correct.** "0 files outside plan.md" and "0 spec commits after the plan" show that the process held. They do not show that the code is right. The retried-wrench bug was still shipped and needed a postmortem and the `A-1` fix (`e161f69`, `7dcb13b`). None of the git measures above counts that bug as a failure.
- **A trailer does not show speed or quality.** A 60% trailer share says who is credited on the commits. It says nothing about speed, quality or how much work a person did. METR's 2025 study of experienced open-source developers found that AI tools made them about 19% slower, even though they believed the tools made them faster. Attribution and productivity are different things.
- **Elapsed time includes waiting.** Commit times are author dates, set by whoever made the commit. Intent to spec includes a night and the approval wait (`54cc768`), and it measures elapsed time, not effort.
